subject: Mobile Development
title: Project Treble: Fixing Updates
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Project Treble: Fixing Updates.

hook.text: Android updates used to take 6 to 18 months to reach most phones. Google tried to fix it.

buildup.text: Project Treble separated the OS framework from hardware-specific vendor code.

discovery.text: This lets Google update the OS without waiting for each chip maker to adapt their drivers.

twist.text: Despite Treble, many manufacturers still delay updates for months to add their own features.

climax.text: Treble improved the situation but didn't solve it. Android updates are still slower than iOS.

punchline.text: Google split the OS in two to speed up updates.

quiz.question: What did Project Treble do?
options: Separated OS framework from vendor-specific code
